concept.title: Spectral radius threshold for fractional ID-$[a,b]$-factor-critical graphs
concept.concept_description: For a graph $G$ with minimum degree $\delta(G) \ge a + r$, if the spectral radius $\lambda(G)$ is at least $a + r + b$, then $G$ is fractional ID-$[a,b]$-factor-critical.
concept.mathematical_framing: For a graph $G$ with minimum degree $\delta(G) \ge a + r$, if the spectral radius $\lambda(G)$ is at least $a + r + b$, then $G$ is fractional ID-$[a,b]$-factor-critical.
concept.lean_guess: 1. Establish that $\lambda(G) \ge a + r + b$ implies sufficient expansion properties via spectral techniques. 2. Show that this expansion guarantees the existence of fractional $[a,b]$-factors in $G-I$ for any independent set $I$ of size $r$. 3. Leverage the minimum degree condition to bound the vertex degrees in $G-I$ within the $[a,b]$ range.

concept.title: Penrose Homology Detects Tait Colorability
concept.concept_description: For any connected trivalent ribbon graph G embedded on a closed surface, the degree-zero Penrose homology group H^{0,*}(G) at the specialization λ = 3 is nonzero if and only if G admits a proper 3-edge coloring (Tait coloring). This refines the classical Penrose criterion—which states P(G;3) > 0 iff G is Tait-colorable—by identifying the specific homological degree that detects colorability, analogous to how Khovanov homology detects the unknot in degree zero.
concept.mathematical_framing: For any connected trivalent ribbon graph G embedded on a closed surface, the degree-zero Penrose homology group H^{0,*}(G) at the specialization λ = 3 is nonzero if and only if G admits a proper 3-edge coloring (Tait coloring). This refines the classical Penrose criterion—which states P(G;3) > 0 iff G is Tait-colorable—by identifying the specific homological degree that detects colorability, analogous to how Khovanov homology detects the unknot in degree zero.
concept.lean_guess: Forward direction: For each Tait coloring c of G, construct an explicit generator of H^{0,*}(G) using the state-sum structure of the Penrose homology cube of resolutions, ensuring distinct colorings yield linearly independent classes. Reverse direction: Show that any nonzero class in H^{0,*}(G) forces the existence of a Tait coloring by analyzing the cobordism maps in the TQFT-valued chain complex and proving that non-colorable graphs have vanishing H^{0,*}. The nonorientable cobordism framework is essential for handling the sign assignments that distinguish colorable from non-colorable configurations.
